From Goethe-Zertifikat B1, practice paper 1, reading

Bohrmaschine statt Roman

Seit dem Frühjahr kann man in der Stadtbücherei einer hessischen Kleinstadt nicht nur Bücher und Filme ausleihen, sondern auch Dinge, die man nur selten braucht: eine Bohrmaschine, ein Zelt, eine Nähmaschine oder einen Beamer für den Filmabend im Garten. Die Idee hatte die Bibliothekarin Sabine Roth.

In diesem Text geht es darum, dass …

  1. eine Bibliothek gebrauchte Geräte verkauft.
  2. Bürger in der Bibliothek kaputte Geräte reparieren.
  3. man in einer Bibliothek auch Gegenstände ausleihen kann.

Every word in a paper can be tapped for its meaning and forms while you practise.

The exams

Which exams the papers cover

There are two practice papers for each of 15 exams: the DTZ, six from the Goethe-Institut, seven from telc gGmbH and TestDaF from the TestDaF-Institut.

ExamWhat it isIn Glossa's papers
DTZThe final language test of the BAMF integration course (Integrationskurs). One test for two levels: depending on the result, a certificate at A2 or B1. Listening, reading, writing, and speaking in pairs.Two papers with the full written part: 20 listening items, 25 reading items and a letter, with the same times. No speaking.
Goethe-Zertifikat A1 to C2Six levels, from A1 (Start Deutsch 1) to C2 (Großes Deutsches Sprachdiplom). From B1 up, four modules (reading, listening, writing, speaking) that are taken and passed separately.Two papers per level. Reading and listening at about half length, writing full length, no speaking.
telc Deutsch A1 to C2Seven exams: A1 (Start Deutsch 1), A2 (Start Deutsch 2), B1 (Zertifikat Deutsch), B2, C1, C1 Hochschule with academic themes, and C2. From B1 to C1, a written part with reading, language elements (Sprachbausteine), listening and writing, and an oral part taken in pairs (at C1 also in threes).Two papers per exam. Shorter reading, language elements and listening, writing full length, no speaking. A paper is judged on the written part alone.
TestDaFThe test for studying at a German university, taken on a computer at a test centre. Reading, listening, writing and speaking, each reported as below TDN 3, TDN 3, TDN 4 or TDN 5 (B2 to C1), with no overall result and no pass mark.Two papers. Shorter reading, four of the seven listening task types, both writing tasks, no speaking, and no TDN levels.

Based on the published exam descriptions, regulations and model papers of g.a.s.t. and the BAMF (DTZ, checked in November 2026) and of the Goethe-Institut, telc gGmbH and the TestDaF-Institut (checked in October 2026). Check them for the current format before your exam.

One level in detail

What the Goethe-Zertifikat B1 asks

The Goethe-Zertifikat B1 has four modules, and each can be taken and retaken on its own and gets its own certificate. Each module is worth 100 points and passes at 60. No dictionaries or other aids are allowed.

ModuleWhat you doIn Glossa's papers
Reading (Lesen)5 parts, 30 items in 65 minutes: a blog post or email, press texts, advertisements matched to situations, reader comments and rules or instructions.All five parts with about half the items, in 33 minutes.
Listening (Hören)4 parts, 30 items in about 40 minutes: short texts, a guided tour or talk, a conversation and a radio discussion. Some parts are played twice, some once.All four parts with about half the items, in 20 minutes.
Writing (Schreiben)3 tasks in 60 minutes: an informal email (about 80 words), a forum post giving your opinion (about 80 words) and a semi-formal email (about 40 words).All three tasks and the full 60 minutes, rated by AI.
Speaking (Sprechen)3 parts in pairs, 15 minutes after 15 minutes of preparation: planning something together, presenting a topic and giving feedback.Not included. Since every module passes on its own, the other three are judged as they would be.

From the Goethe-Institut's exam regulations and B1 model paper, checked in October 2026.

The integration course

What the DTZ asks

The Deutsch-Test für Zuwanderer (DTZ) is the final language test of the German integration course, which the Federal Office for Migration and Refugees (BAMF) runs; since 1 January 2023 g.a.s.t. e.V. has organised and marked it on the BAMF's behalf. It is taken at test centres the BAMF authorises, usually integration course providers. Glossa's papers follow the version for adults.

The written part takes 100 minutes without a break; the oral part, in pairs with two examiners, follows, usually on the same day. No dictionaries are allowed.

PartWhat you doIn Glossa's papers
Listening (Hören)4 parts, 20 items, about 25 minutes, 20 points: phone messages, announcements, short radio items, everyday conversations and three people's opinions on one topic. Every text is played once.All 20 items in 25 minutes. Recordings can be replayed.
Reading (Lesen)5 parts, 25 items, 45 minutes, 25 points: a directory, advertisements matched to situations, short press texts and notices, a brochure or instructions, and a formal letter with gaps.All 25 items in 45 minutes.
Writing (Schreiben)30 minutes, 20 points: a semi-formal or formal letter or email, one of two tasks, with four points to write about.One task in 30 minutes, rated by AI against the four published criteria.
Speaking (Sprechen)About 16 minutes in pairs, 100 points: introducing yourself, talking about a picture and your own experience, and planning something with your partner.Not included: Glossa cannot yet assess free speech the way an examiner does.

From g.a.s.t.'s DTZ pages and the BAMF's rules, checked in November 2026.

DTZ results

How the DTZ level is set, and what B1 gives you

Listening and reading are added together (out of 45); writing (out of 20) and speaking (out of 100) are rated separately. The B1 bands start at 33 of 45, 15 of 20 and 75 of 100; the A2 bands at 20, 7 and 35.

  • No certificate at all without at least A2 in speaking.
  • A2: at least A2 in speaking, and at least A2 in listening and reading or in writing.
  • B1, for tests from 1 November 2026: B1 in two of the three results, one of which must be speaking, and at least A2 in the third.
  • B1 in the DTZ together with a pass in Leben in Deutschland gives the Zertifikat Integrationskurs, which counts as proof of German for extending a residence permit, for a settlement permit (Niederlassungserlaubnis) and for naturalisation, which requires B1.
  • Glossa's DTZ papers pass at the B1 bands: 33 of 45 for listening and reading together, 15 of 20 for writing. Without speaking they cannot give an overall level.
  • The test can be retaken any number of times, always in full: no part result is carried over.

Studying in Germany

What TestDaF results mean for university

TestDaF is not passed or failed. Each of the four sections gets its own result, and the certificate does not expire.

  • Universities set their own requirements. The usual one is TDN 4 in all four sections.
  • A university may accept less or ask for more in a single skill, so check the requirement of the course you are applying to.
  • Glossa's TestDaF papers show the share of points only. The TestDaF-Institut does not publish a way to turn practice scores into TDN levels, so Glossa does not convert them.

Honest limits

How the practice papers differ from the real exams

  • No grade or level is given. A paper shows the share of points. Where the exam passes at 60%, a paper applies that mark to the parts it has, but it cannot tell you which grade, result or TDN level you would get.
  • Reading and listening are shorter than in the real Goethe, telc and TestDaF exams, usually about half the items with the time cut to match. Some task types are left out, such as three of TestDaF's listening task types and the book review in Goethe C2.
  • There is no speaking part. Where an exam's pass rule includes speaking, the paper is judged on the written part alone. The DTZ papers have the full written part, and Glossa has no Leben in Deutschland test.
  • Recordings can be replayed, and synthetic voices read them: one voice with the speakers' names in the Goethe, telc and TestDaF papers, two alternating voices in the DTZ conversations. Play each one as often as the real exam does, and then answer.
  • Words can be tapped for their meaning while you practise; the real exams allow no dictionary.

Questions

Common questions

Is Glossa connected with the BAMF, g.a.s.t., the Goethe-Institut, telc or the TestDaF-Institut?
No. Glossa is not affiliated with or endorsed by any of them. The papers follow their published exam descriptions and model papers, with original content.
Should I take Goethe or telc?
Glossa has papers for both at every level from A1 to C2. If you attend an integration course, it ends with the DTZ. Otherwise, whoever asks you for a certificate, such as an employer, a university or an authority, decides which exams and levels they accept, so check with them. TestDaF is made for people who want to study at a German university.
Can a practice paper tell me whether I would pass?
No. The papers are shorter than the real exams, have no speaking part, and writing is rated by AI, so the score is a guide to what to work on, not a prediction.
What is free?
The whole German course from A1 to C1, the grammar reference and word practice are free. The exam practice papers, conversation practice, stories and the other extras are part of Premium.
I speak Russian, Finnish or Ukrainian. Is there a course for me?
Yes. German for Russian speakers, German for Finnish speakers and German for Ukrainian speakers have the same exam papers, with the instructions and explanations in Russian, Finnish or Ukrainian.
